svg.title: Week 11 concurrency roadmap
svg.desc: A vertical causal roadmap from shared process resources and private thread state through races, mutexes, condition variables, atomics, liveness, cache effects, and evidence-driven debugging.
svg.text: Threads and concurrency: one causal path
Each mechanism answers the failure exposed immediately above it.
1 | shared process, private execution state
shared: address space | heap | file table | signal dispositions
per thread: registers | user/kernel stacks | TLS | blocked mask
2 | conflicting accesses expose races
no happens-before -> undefined behavior; interleavings are only one symptom
compiler transformations happen before CPU execution and coherence
3 | mutex and futex protect an invariant
uncontended: userspace atomic fast path | contended: futex wait / wake
ownership and global lock order constrain who may proceed
4 | condition wait closes the sleep gap
predicate loop under mutex -> atomic unlock + sleep -> relock + recheck
bounded queue alternates empty, occupied, and full states
5 | atomics separate atomicity from ordering
relaxed modification order | release/acquire publication | seq_cst total order
message passing selects the edge required by the payload
6 | correct programs can still fail to progress or scale
wait-for cycle -> deadlock | unfair choice -> starvation
shared cache line -> coherence traffic | private lines -> scalable work
7 | debug by comparing independent evidence
assertions | sanitizer / Helgrind | GDB | perf: each answers a different question
identify -> reproduce -> classify layer -> compare evidence -> diagnose or SKIP
